Hong Kong Technology Hardware Firm Expands Production Capacity with HK$200 Million Investment

Hong Kong’s technology hardware sector is set for a boost as Advance Optix Ltd has announced a HK$200 million investment to expand its manufacturing facilities in the New Territories. The move underscores continued confidence in Hong Kong as a regional technology hub and is expected to create over 120 technical and engineering jobs over the next two years.

Advance Optix, a key supplier of optoelectronic components for the Asia-Pacific market, will increase its production floor by 40% and invest in new automated assembly lines. The company cited rising demand for high-speed data transmission hardware from telecom and cloud service providers as a driving factor.

“We are responding to strong customer demand and leveraging Hong Kong’s skilled workforce,” said Eric Man, CEO of Advance Optix. “This expansion will enhance our agility in serving both regional and global customers.”

The Hong Kong Productivity Council welcomed the investment, noting its alignment with government initiatives to promote innovation and advanced manufacturing. “Advance Optix’s commitment reflects the resilience and competitiveness of Hong Kong’s technology hardware sector,” said Dr. Emily Yuen, Director of Industry Promotion at the Council.

Industry analysts see the expansion as a positive signal amid global supply chain recalibrations. “Hong Kong’s robust logistics infrastructure and proximity to key electronics markets make it an attractive base for technology hardware firms seeking to scale up,” commented Kelvin Wong, senior analyst at Asia Tech Insights.

Construction on the expanded facility is scheduled to begin in September, with initial production lines expected to come online by mid-2025. Advance Optix also revealed plans to collaborate with local universities on workforce training and R&D projects, supporting the development of next-generation photonics and connectivity devices.

The Hong Kong Electronics Association estimates that the city’s technology hardware sector recorded a 7% growth in output last year. With new investments like Advance Optix’s, industry leaders anticipate further strengthening of Hong Kong’s role in the global electronics supply chain.
